measure_name: Climate-informed policy, regulation and sector standards
definition: Climate-informed policy, regulation and sector standards establish formal rules or frameworks that require climate resilience, adaptation or emissions reduction to be incorporated into future investments or operations. Counts when the project finances the development, revision, adoption or implementation of a policy, regulation, code, mandatory standard or formal sector planning framework with explicit climate-related provisions. The intervention must change the governing framework rather than merely apply a technical requirement to one project-financed asset. Project-level technical specifications belong to the underlying technical measure, not climate_governance. Does not count for Paris Alignment commitments, CCDR recommendations, CDRS findings, references to national climate strategies, generic institutional strengthening, training, studies, voluntary aspirations or existing policies cited only as context. The rule must apply beyond this project's financed assets and be formally adopted: rules for all future facilities of an agency count; a guideline written only for this project's rollout does not. Formal continuity rules for an institution or sector belong here; a recovery plan for a specific system is disaster_recovery.
boundary: The project changes formal sector rules governing future investments or operations.
note: Narrowed to formal sector-level governance interventions. A requirement in a bidding document to flood-proof one facility is resilient_infrastructure_design, not climate_governance. A project financing development of a national flood-resilient infrastructure code is climate_governance. v4 (2026-10-20): Dev's revision; measures are defined by the intervention, the asset map gives the asset. v5 (2026-10-21): grade 1 adds existing systems, results-framework indicators, economic-analysis assumptions and other World Bank projects; types rewritten to exclude each other and asked as one choice. v6 (2026-10-21, Dev's graded sheet): hedged wording is grade 2; benefit claims, examples and other donors are grade 1; boundary lines from the graders' notes; commit_floor from the graded sheet. v7 (2026-10-21, Dev's s4 sheet and a review of it): scales say how examples, technical assistance, training and hedges grade; the scope test (beyond this project's assets, formally adopted) and continuity rules against disaster recovery.
